etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English destroyen, from Old French destruire, Vulgar Latin *destrugō, from Classical Latin dēstruō, from dē- (“un-, de-”) + struō (“I build”).

definitions.definition: (transitive, intransitive) To damage beyond use or repair; to damage (something) to the point that it effectively ceases to exist.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, John 2:19:
quote.text: Iesus answered, and said vnto them, Destroy this temple, and in three dayes I will raise it vp.

quote.citation: 1972 November 5, Joan Lee Faust, “AROUND THE Garden”, in The New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: Repeated use of this type of [water] on plants results in deflocculation[] of the soil. Good quality soil consists of loose aggregates which provide natural aeration and ease of root run. Sodium accumulation in soil destroys this natural flocculation and causes the soil to pack.

quote.citation: 2013, Steven McLaughlin, Clubland UK: On the Door in the Rave Era:
quote.text: Krav is a martial art of last resort that assumes no quarter and focuses purely on disarming, disabling and, if necessary, destroying your opponent.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To neutralize, undo a property or condition.
(transitive) To severely disrupt the well-being of (a person); ruin.

quote.citation: 2005, Kliatt Young Adult Paperback Book Guide:
quote.text: Other girls in the foster home are eager to destroy her and get her kicked out of the place. It's a tough situation.

definitions.definition: (transitive, informal) To utterly defeat; to crush.

quote.citation: 2012 November 11, Sam Anderson, “The Oklahoma City Thunder’s Fairy-Tale Rise”, in The New York Times‎[2], New York, N.Y.: The New York Times Company, →ISSN, →OCLC, archived from the original on 2023-04-10:
quote.text: Growing up, [Kevin] Durant told me, he was a sore loser. That all changed one day when he was 11, after he got destroyed by his father in a game of one on one in the driveway.

definitions.definition: (transitive, bodybuilding, slang, antiphrasis) To exhaust completely and thus recreate or build up.
(transitive, slang, vulgar) To penetrate sexually in an aggressive way.
(transitive, US, slang) To sing a song extremely poorly.

quote.citation: 2001, Jeff Nathanson, Rush Hour 2‎[3], New Line Cinema:
quote.text: JAMES CARTER: The man's destroying a classic!

definitions.definition: (transitive, slang) To eat food quickly, hungrily or completely.
